The third season of *Girls* received positive reviews. On [Metacritic](/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the third season of the series holds an average of 76 based on 18 reviews.[[67]](#cite_note-metacritic3-67) [Rotten Tomatoes](/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") reports a 91% approval rating from critics, based on 32 reviews with an [average score](/wiki/Weighted_mean "Weighted mean") of 7.9/10. The consensus states: "Still rife with shock value, Season 3 of *Girls* also benefits from an increasingly mature tone."[[83]](#cite_note-83)

Tim Goodman of *[The Hollywood Reporter](/wiki/The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* lauded the first two episodes, and commented: "Going into its third season, Girls is as refreshing and audacious as ever and one of the few half-hour dramedies where you can feel its heart pounding and see its belly ripple with laughter."[[84]](#cite_note-84) In addition, *[The New York Times](/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, *[Entertainment Weekly](/wiki/Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")* and *[PopMatters](/wiki/PopMatters "PopMatters")* praised the comedic portrayal of its lead female characters.[[85]](#cite_note-85)[[86]](#cite_note-86)[[87]](#cite_note-87)

The fourth season of *Girls* received generally positive reviews. On [Metacritic](/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), the fourth season of the series holds an average of 75 based on 16 reviews.[[69]](#cite_note-metacritic4-69) [Rotten Tomatoes](/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") reports an 83% approval rating from critics, based on 24 reviews with an [average score](/wiki/Weighted_mean "Weighted mean") of 7.5/10. The consensus states: "*Girls* is familiar after four seasons, but its convoluted-yet-comical depiction of young women dealing with the real world still manages to impress."[[88]](#cite_note-88)

fanoutqa_016148.x:
Elon Musk :: Business career :: Tesla :: SolarCity and Tesla Energy :: chunk_0012
Main articles: [SolarCity](/wiki/SolarCity "SolarCity") and [Tesla Energy](/wiki/Tesla_Energy "Tesla Energy")

Musk provided the initial concept and financial capital for [SolarCity](/wiki/SolarCity "SolarCity"), which his cousins [Lyndon](/wiki/Lyndon_Rive "Lyndon Rive") and Peter Rive founded in 2006.[[150]](#cite_note-154) By 2013, SolarCity was the second largest provider of solar power systems in the United States.[[151]](#cite_note-155) In 2014, Musk promoted the idea of SolarCity building an advanced production facility in [Buffalo](/wiki/Buffalo,_New_York "Buffalo, New York"), New York, triple the size of the largest solar plant in the United States.[[152]](#cite_note-156) Construction of [the factory](/wiki/Gigafactory_New_York "Gigafactory New York") started in 2014 and was completed in 2017. It operated as a joint venture with [Panasonic](/wiki/Panasonic "Panasonic") until early 2020.[[153]](#cite_note-157)[[154]](#cite_note-158)

Tesla acquired SolarCity for $2 billion in 2016 (equivalent to $2,700,000,000 in 2025) and merged it with its battery unit to create [Tesla Energy](/wiki/Tesla_Energy "Tesla Energy"). The deal's announcement resulted in a more than 10% drop in Tesla's stock price; at the time, SolarCity was facing liquidity issues.[[155]](#cite_note-:5-159) Multiple shareholder groups filed a lawsuit against Musk and Tesla's directors, stating that the purchase of SolarCity was done solely to benefit Musk and came at the expense of Tesla and its shareholders.[[156]](#cite_note-160)[[157]](#cite_note-161) Tesla directors settled the lawsuit in January 2020, leaving Musk the sole remaining defendant.[[158]](#cite_note-162)[[159]](#cite_note-163) Two years later, the court ruled in Musk's favor.[[155]](#cite_note-:5-159)

On his eleventh birthday, Harry discovers he is a wizard when [Rubeus Hagrid](/wiki/Rubeus_Hagrid "Rubeus Hagrid") brings him an acceptance letter from [Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry](/wiki/Hogwarts_School_of_Witchcraft_and_Wizardry "Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry"). Harry learns that his parents, [James](/wiki/James_Potter_(character) "James Potter (character)") and [Lily Potter](/wiki/Lily_Potter "Lily Potter"), were murdered by a powerful Dark wizard, [Lord Voldemort](/wiki/Lord_Voldemort "Lord Voldemort"), who also tried to kill Harry. However, Voldemort's [killing curse](/wiki/Avada_Kedavra "Avada Kedavra") bounced back and apparently destroyed him, leaving Harry with a lightning-bolt-shaped scar on his forehead. Due to his miraculous survival, Harry became famous among wizards.

Hagrid takes Harry to [Diagon Alley](/wiki/Diagon_Alley "Diagon Alley") to shop for school supplies. Harry buys a wand, and the proprietor tells him that his wand and Voldemort's wand contain feathers from the same [phoenix](/wiki/Phoenix_(mythology) "Phoenix (mythology)"). [![Mars circling the Sun further and slower than Earth](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cc/Solar_system_orrery_inner_planets.gif/330px-Solar_system_orrery_inner_planets.gif)](/wiki/File:Solar_system_orrery_inner_planets.gif)

Orbit of Mars and other Inner Solar System planets

Mars's average distance from the Sun is roughly 230 million km (143 million mi), and its orbital period is 687 (Earth) days. The solar day (or [sol](/wiki/Mars_sol "Mars sol")) on Mars is only slightly longer than an Earth day: 24 hours, 39 minutes, and 35.244 seconds.[[199]](#cite_note-201) A Martian year is equal to 1.8809 Earth years, or 1 year, 320 days, and 18.2 hours.[[2]](#cite_note-NasaFactSheet-3) The [gravitational potential](/wiki/Gravitational_potential "Gravitational potential") difference and thus the [delta-v needed](/wiki/Delta-v_budget "Delta-v budget") to transfer between Mars and Earth is the second lowest for Earth.[[200]](#cite_note-Petropoulos_Longuski_Bonfiglio_2000_pp._776–783-202)[[201]](#cite_note-Taylor_2020-203)

The axial tilt of Mars is 25.19° relative to its [orbital plane](/wiki/Orbital_plane "Orbital plane"), which is similar to the [axial tilt of Earth](/wiki/Ecliptic#Obliquity_of_the_ecliptic "Ecliptic").[[2]](#cite_note-NasaFactSheet-3) As a result, Mars has seasons like Earth, though on Mars they are nearly twice as long because its orbital period is that much longer. In the present day, the orientation of the [north pole](/wiki/North_pole "North pole") of Mars is close to the star [Deneb](/wiki/Deneb "Deneb").[[21]](#cite_note-barlow08-23)

Mars has a relatively pronounced [orbital eccentricity](/wiki/Orbital_eccentricity "Orbital eccentricity") of about 0.09; of the seven other planets in the Solar System, only [Mercury](/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (p

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4f/Moons_of_solar_system_v7.jpg/500px-Moons_of_solar_system_v7.jpg)](/wiki/File:Moons_of_solar_system_v7.jpg)

Size comparison of the main moons of the Solar System with Earth to scale. Nineteen moons are large enough [to be round](/wiki/Hydrostatic_equilibrium "Hydrostatic equilibrium"), several having [subsurface oceans](/wiki/Subsurface_ocean "Subsurface ocean") and one, [Titan](/wiki/Titan_(moon) "Titan (moon)"), having a considerable atmosphere.

The Moon is the fifth largest (by size and mass) natural satellite of the Solar System. It is categorizable as a [planetary-mass moon](/wiki/Planetary-mass_moon "Planetary-mass moon"), making it a satellite planet under the [geophysical definitions of the term](/wiki/Geophysical_definition_of_planet "Geophysical definition of planet").[[18]](#cite_note-Metzger2021-24) It is smaller than [Mercury](/wiki/Mercury_(planet) "Mercury (planet)") but considerably larger than the largest [dwarf planet](/wiki/Dwarf_planet "Dwarf planet") of the Solar System, [Pluto](/wiki/Pluto "Pluto"). The Moon is the largest natural satellite in the Solar System relative to its [primary](/wiki/Primary_(astronomy) "Primary (astronomy)") planet.[[g]](#cite_note-78)[[h]](#cite_note-Moon_vs._Charon-79)[[72]](#cite_note-80)

[Legislative](/wiki/Legislature "Legislature") functions are administered by the pope, but are also delegated to the [Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State](/wiki/Pontifical_Commission_for_Vatican_City_State "Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State"), led by the [president of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State](/wiki/President_of_the_Pontifical_Commission_for_Vatican_City_State "President of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State"). Its members are cardinals appointed by the pope for terms of five years.Acts of the commission must be approved by the Pope, through the Holy See's [Secretariat of State](/wiki/Secretariat_of_State_(Holy_See) "Secretariat of State (Holy See)"), and must be published in a special appendix of the *[Acta Apostolicae Sedis](/wiki/Acta_Apostolicae_Sedis "Acta Apostolicae Sedis")*.Most of the content of this appendix consists of routine executive decrees, such as approval for a new set of postage stamps.

[Executive authority](/wiki/Executive_(government) "Executive (government)") is delegated to the president of the Governorate of Vatican City, who is also the president of the Pontificial Commission. **Nicholas David Nurse** (born July 24, 1967) is an American professional [basketball](/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") coach and former player who is the head coach for the [Philadelphia 76ers](/wiki/Philadelphia_76ers "Philadelphia 76ers") of the [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA). He previously served as head coach for the [Toronto Raptors](/wiki/Toronto_Raptors "Toronto Raptors"), whom he led to an [NBA championship](/wiki/NBA_championship "NBA championship") in 2019 and with whom he was named the [NBA Coach of the Year](/wiki/NBA_Coach_of_the_Year "NBA Coach of the Year") in 2020.

Nurse played [college basketball](/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [Northern Iowa Panthers](/wiki/Northern_Iowa_Panthers_men%27s_basketball "Northern Iowa Panthers men's basketball"). He played professional basketball with the [Derby Rams](/wiki/Derby_Rams "Derby Rams") in the [British Basketball League](/wiki/British_Basketball_League "British Basketball League").

Nicholas David Nurse was born on July 24, 1967, in [Carroll, Iowa](/wiki/Carroll,_Iowa "Carroll, Iowa").[[1]](#cite_note-UNI-1)[[2]](#cite_note-ourselves-2) Nurse attended [Kuemper Catholic School System](/wiki/Kuemper_Catholic_School_System "Kuemper Catholic School System"), where he excelled in [basketball](/wiki/Basketball "Basketball").

On November 13, 2006, YouTube was purchased by Google for 1.65 billion [USD](/wiki/United_States_dollar "United States dollar") (equivalent to $2.44 billion in 2025).[[12]](#cite_note-12) Google expanded YouTube's business model from generating revenue through [advertisements](/wiki/Advertising "Advertising") alone to paid offerings such as [movies](/wiki/YouTube_TV "YouTube TV") and [exclusive programming](/wiki/List_of_YouTube_Premium_original_programming "List of YouTube Premium original programming") explicitly produced for YouTube. It also offers [YouTube Premium](/wiki/YouTube_Premium "YouTube Premium"), a paid subscription option for watching videos without ads. YouTube incorporated the [Google AdSense](/wiki/Google_AdSense "Google AdSense") program, generating more revenue for both YouTube and approved users. In 2023, YouTube's advertising revenue totaled $31.7 billion, a 2% increase from the $31.1 billion reported in 2022.[[13]](#cite_note-:0-13) From Q4 2023 to Q3 2024, YouTube's combined revenue from advertising and subscriptions exceeded $50 billion.[[14]](#cite_note-14)
